checks.title: The whole draw fits a USB 2.0 port
checks.detail: At most 270.5 mA from USB at the sensor's 205 mA pulse (Pico 30 mA allowance + the 3.3 V load counted 1:1), vs 500 mA from a USB 2.0 port; about 62.5 mA on average

checks.title: The micro-USB plug seats through the side opening
checks.detail: The 11 x 8 mm moulding has 0.75 and 0.75 mm each side in the opening (at least 0.3); seated, it goes 1.50 mm into the wall

checks.title: The printed walls meet the print shops' least walls
checks.detail: shell walls 2 mm, lid 2 mm (FDM: 1 mm least, 2 mm for a part up to 100 mm; this case is 64 mm); round fasteners insert columns 2.00 mm, Pico standoffs 1.65 mm, sensor standoffs 1.65 mm, OLED bosses 1.65 mm (more than 1.5 mm asked)

checks.title: Regulatory standards
checks.detail: Built for your own desk it needs nothing. Selling it in the EU would need CE marking (EMC directive for the electronics, RoHS) and in the US FCC Part 15B; the Pico's own compliance doesn't cover the finished product. It is not a certified CO2 measuring instrument.

checks.title: Every part the design needs is in the BOM
The 3.3 V load fits the Pico's regulator
checks.detail: Peak external load on 3V3(OUT): sensor 205 + OLED 29 + LED 6.5 = 240.5 mA, under the 300 mA the Pico datasheet asks (59.5 mA to spare)

checks.title: The LED's current suits the GPIO and the LED
checks.detail: 390 ohm: red 3.46 mA, green 3.08 mA at typical Vf, 2.05 mA at the 2.5 V maximum Vf; each under the RP2040's 4 mA default drive and the LED's 30 mA, and at least 1 mA so it lights

checks.title: The GPIO bank's total current stays in the RP2040's limit
checks.detail: 6.54 mA sourced by GPIOs (both colours on) vs 50 mA for all of IOVDD

checks.title: The pins are distinct and do what they are wired for
checks.detail: I2C0 SDA GP4, SCL GP5; LED red GP14 (PWM 7A), green GP15 (PWM 7B)

checks.title: The I2C devices have their own addresses and the bus speed suits them
checks.detail: SCD4x at 0x62, OLED at 0x3c or 0x3d; bus at 100 kHz, the SCD4x takes up to 400 kHz

checks.title: The light's thresholds sit inside the sensor's specified range
checks.detail: Green below 1000 ppm, red from 2000 ppm (UBA guide values); the SCD40 is specified to 2000 ppm, reading +-150.0 ppm at 2000

checks.title: The window shows the whole active area from 30 degrees off axis, and only glass
checks.detail: Window half-size 12.20 x 6.75 mm vs 12.03 x 6.59 mm needed for 30 degrees through the 2 mm wall; glass edges 13.35 mm to the sides, 7.53 above and 11.73 below the window's centre

checks.title: The LED clears the OLED and the top wall
checks.detail: Flange 1.85 mm above the OLED board, 1.60 mm under the top wall (at least 0.3)

checks.title: Every screw bites far enough and stops short of a face
checks.detail: M3 lid screws 4.00 mm in (at least 3, room 7.00); M2 Pico screws 5.00 mm in (at least 2, room 5.20); M2 sensor screws 4.80 mm in (at least 2, room 8.70); M2 OLED screws 2.40 mm in (at least 2, room 2.75)

checks.title: The CO2 sensor sits below the heat sources (Sensirion's advice)
checks.detail: The sensor's board starts 1.1 mm above the Pico, so the Pico's warmth (about 0.1 W) rises past it. Chosen so the USB plug sits low (a cable pull tips it less); the CO2 reading is compensated inside the SCD40, but the temperature and humidity it shows need TEMP_OFFSET_C set against a thermometer (assembly, last step)

checks.title: The sensor's self-calibration gets fresh air
checks.detail: The SCD40's automatic self-calibration assumes it sees outdoor air (about 400 ppm) for 3 minutes at least once every 7 days. A room that is never aired drifts the zero; air it, or put the monitor on an open window sill now and then
